tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Prefer it to 'screenshot' to find what to tap (tap a frame's center), read text, or check a control's state or value; use 'screenshot' for layout, color, and images. Default: the whole visible tree; x/y: the element under that point with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container); marker: the first element whose label (or match_key) contains that text. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted, and text longer than its area shows is cut and ends with ... (occlusion and transparency are not detected); a tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with x/y or marker; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring. Omit for the whole tree, or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type).

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. See In Progress). Previous: 2026-08-18 (zimmTokens.ts made fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files instead of hand-retyped literals; `zimmButton.css.ts` established as the single source of truth for button styling, `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*` class system removed; `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem for WCAG 1.4.4; `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` token convention; new `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the resulting styling-source hierarchy. ## What's Complete

- **Token architecture hardened** (2026-08-18): `zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry) is now fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files via imports instead of hand-duplicated literals, closing the drift risk the original port above carried. `typography.ts` gained a proper `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights` scale layer. `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem (WCAG 1.4.4); within those two files, px is kept only for hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets — now named tokens in `spacing.ts`'s `focusRingOffsets`). `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding constants are a separate, already-flagged px exception (not hairline geometry) — see below. `zimmButton.css.ts` is now the single source of truth for button styling — `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*`/`.zimm-text-btn-*` classes (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states) were removed entirely; any button must use Chakra's `<Button>`, never a class. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` convention (no direct `foundation/` imports, no Chakra semantic colour-token names). New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the styling-source hierarchy, unit rules, the alias-is-a-reference-not-a-copy principle, and a real gotcha: importing an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path resolves correctly in the real app but silently renders the unstyled base version in Storybook/Vitest (the `ccExtensibility` resolver is webpack-only, neither tool loads it). Still open, flagged inline rather than silently resolved: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px prototype values) disagree with the Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all — both pending UI-designer sign-off.
- **Header override** (`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`): two-row layout, brand logo via `BrandLogo` component (overrides base SVG at `overrides/app/assets/svg/brand-logo.svg`), uppercase nav with `::after` hover animation, Account/Saved/Bag text buttons with matching animation, chevrons hidden. Still being refined visually against Figma.
- Path aliases (`~` → root, `app` → `overrides/app`) wired up across Babel, tsconfig, Storybook, and Jest
- **Per-tier environment switching** (`npm run env` → `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`) — manages `.env.shared` / `.env.<tier>` across dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod via `init` (scaffold + pull + Contentful auto-fetch), `validate [--live]` (structural checks plus live Contentful Delivery API + SFCC SLAS guest-token calls), and `push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only). Shared/tier values (excluding personal credentials) can be centrally published through this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per tier) — write gated to repo Admin. Landed 2026-07-13.

## What's Pending

New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.

- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

1	*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
2	
3	## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
4	
5	- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
6	  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
7	  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
8	  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
9	  runs its tests."
10	- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
11	  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
12	  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
13	  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
14	  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
15	- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
16	  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
17	  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
18	  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
19	  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
20	  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
21	  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
22	  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
23	  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
24	  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
25	  skipped) regardless of its title.
26	- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
27	  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
28	  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
29	- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
30	  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
31	  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
32	- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
33	  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
34	  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
35	  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
36	  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
37	
38

*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*

## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)

- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
  runs its tests."
- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
  skipped) regardless of its title.
- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.

**Why, precisely (this is the deeper finding vs. the earlier version of this memory):**

1. **Jira ground truth on sprints** (board 500 "SFCC board"): **SFCC Sprint 1** (goal: "Configure
   SFCC foundations and deliver the global UI shell with homepage ready for the next build phase")
   ran 2026-07-06 → **closed 2026-07-26**. **SFCC Sprint 2 is active now**, 2026-07-28 → 2026-08-10.
   Sprint 3 starts 2026-08-10. **`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`'s sprint table is stale/wrong** —
   it's a 2026-06-23 draft that still labels "Current position" as "Sprint 0," and its dates
   (Sprint 1 = 29 Jun–10 Jul, Sprint 3 = 27 Jul–7 Aug) don't match the real Jira board by several
   days. Don't cite sprintScope.md's dates for real sprint boundaries — pull the live board instead.
2. **Sprint 1 already closed calendar-wise, but the epic that owns platform/CI-CD setup did not
   close with it.** `SFCC-1` ("Platform Setup & Environments," explicit scope includes "CI/CD
   pipeline including... bundle size gate, Playwright P0 suite, Lighthouse CI") is **still "In
   Progress"**, last updated today. That's the substantive reason no release branch got cut at
   Sprint 1's close — the foundation work the Branching Guide's "when a sprint is complete" trigger
   assumes was ready, wasn't actually done yet.
3. **The concrete blockers are tracked and still open**, not hidden: Confluence "[7.1c CI/CD &
   Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530)"
   (v2) lists "Configure `release/**` branch protection" as **⬜, owner Integration Lead**, plus a
   long list of still-⬜ SIT-environment items (GitHub `sit` environment not created, `MRT_SIT_URL`/
   `COMMERCE_API_*_SIT` secrets unset, MRT project slug unconfirmed in `mobify.config.js`).
4. **Environment stand-up work is live right now, same day.** `SFCC-254` ("Environment Setup - DEV,
   TEST, SIT & UAT for All Storefronts," Sprint 2 ticket, In Progress) got a comment today
   (2026-08-03 20:17, Victor T. Crisostomo): *"Deployment done on UAT. Core/Vendor data imported...
   Sample data and MRT working on test environment. Checking on SIT MRT environment."* — i.e. SIT
   MRT still isn't confirmed working as of this afternoon. Five follow-on tickets (SFCC-259..263,
   "Deploy to UAT: Base Category/Pricebook/Product Catalogue/Inventory List/8 Storefronts Setup")
   are queued **To Do**, blocked on SFCC-254 — but these are **SFCC/Business-Manager config
   deployments** (a different backend repo/process), not this PWA repo's `release/*` branch flow.
   Easy to conflate the two if a scrum master hears "deploying to UAT" from the SFCC side.
5. **Confluence "[Branching Guide (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)"**
   (v3, canonical source AGENTS.md/`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` are built from) says release
   branches are "created by squad leads or CI from a tagged `develop` state... developers do not
   create these," tagged via **`scripts/tagRelease.sh`** (exists in repo, confirmed) run from `main`
   *after* the release PR merges (creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` tags).
   Separately, `deploy-dev.yml` has a dormant **`tag-sprint`** job that auto-tags `sprint/{N}/{date}`
   whenever `scripts/sprint.txt` changes on `develop` — **but `scripts/sprint.txt` doesn't exist in
   the repo yet**, so this has never fired either (`git tag -l` confirms zero `sprint/*` tags). If
   the scrum master expected *some* automatic tag/branch to appear at a sprint boundary, this
   inert-but-wired mechanism is a plausible source of that expectation.
6. **Open, unresolved decision that should land before the first release branch is cut:** draft
   Confluence proposal "[Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656)"
   (v18, still "Draft — for review by squad leads + Integration lead," still has an unresolved
   Open Question 3 about whether `deploy-sit.yml` becomes tag-triggered) would **replace**
   `scripts/tagRelease.sh` with `npm version`-based tagging entirely. Deciding this first avoids
   cutting the first real release under a tagging convention that gets retired a sprint later.

**How to apply:** If asked again whether the release branch exists/is "already set up" — answer is
still **no**. Frame it as *on track, not overdue*: the Branching Guide's own trigger ("sprint
complete + something ready to promote") hasn't fully fired yet, because the epic that delivers the
prerequisites (`SFCC-1`) is still open, and the concrete missing pieces (release/** branch
protection, SIT secrets/environment, `mobify.config.js`) are already tracked on 7.1c owned by
Integration Lead, not undiscovered gaps. Natural next checkpoint is Sprint 2's close (2026-08-10) —

content.content:
1	# PRD – Checkout (Confirmed Scope)
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Checkout Flow and Delivery", "Order Management", and "Payments". Last updated: 2026-06-25.*
4	
5	## 1. Purpose
6	
7	Define the confirmed checkout behaviour for the SFCC PWA frontend. This document excludes speculative or future capabilities. Requirements IDs (CFD-xxx, OM-xxx, PAY-xxx) reference the signed-off requirements spreadsheet.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 2. Supported Checkout Types
12	
13	- ✅ Guest Checkout (email address only; no forced account creation)
14	- ✅ Registered Customer Checkout
15	- ✅ Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (Buy Online, Pick Up in Store) — both guest and registered
16	- ✅ Order on Behalf Of (OOBO) — CS agents in Business Manager (see section 13)
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 3. Checkout Entry Rules (CFD-001 – CFD-014)
21	
22	Anonymous users are shown a checkout entry screen with:
23	- Guest checkout option (email required only) (CFD-007)
24	- Registered login option (email + password) (CFD-001)
25	- Trust messaging: Free Returns, Fast Shipping, Secure Payments (CFD-003)
26	
27	No separate login page — login is inline on the checkout entry screen per new UX designs (CFD-001, signed-off update). Reducing login friction at the checkout entry page is in scope for launch.
28	
29	Authenticated users within a 7-day validity window skip checkout entry entirely and are routed directly into checkout. The 7-day window is configurable (CFD-002).
30	
31	Password reset is supported from the checkout entry page. If reset is initiated from checkout, redirect customer back to checkout to continue; if from My Account, redirect back to My Account (CFD-004).
32	
33	Saved delivery addresses, billing addresses, and payment methods are pre-populated at the relevant checkout steps for authenticated customers (CFD-005). Active session bag merges with any saved bag on login during checkout, retaining all items (CFD-006). Email address and previously entered delivery details are preserved if the customer exits and returns to checkout (CFD-010).
34	
35	Marketing opt-in checkbox at checkout entry — unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (CFD-009). Guest opt-ins go to Emarsys via Omneo. Omneo is the system of record for customer identity, loyalty, and clienteling; SFCC syncs bidirectionally via MuleSoft webhooks (CFD-012). Customer authentication uses SFCC Configurable account management; passwords are not migrated from Magento, so all existing customers must reset at go-live (CFD-013).
36	
37	Checkout entry behaviour is consistent across all domestic storefronts — no market-specific variations in authentication or guest flow (CFD-014).
38	
39	**Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (overrides original CFD-011, which is now strikethrough). Implementation details still Open — see Open Items.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 4. Checkout Steps (CFD-022)
44	
45	Two delivery modes; steps differ. Home Delivery is selected by default (CFD-022):
46	
47	### Home Delivery
48	1. Delivery address
49	2. Delivery method
50	3. Billing address
51	4. Order review + payment
52	5. Order confirmation
53	
54	### Collect in Boutique (BOPIS)
55	1. Boutique selection (Google Maps interactive map; alphabetical; outlets at bottom)
56	2. Collection name (first + last; must match ID; not pre-populated at launch)
57	3. Order review + payment
58	4. Order confirmation
59	
60	Packaging choice (Eco or Signature; no cost impact) is presented at the delivery step for both modes (CFD-054). Default option and available options configurable per storefront in Business Manager.
61	
62	*Open: whether billing address is a required step in the BOPIS flow is not explicitly stated. Clarify before implementing.*
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 5. Order Summary (CFD-015 – CFD-021)
67	
68	- Per line item: product image, name, price (was/now if on sale), size, quantity (CFD-015)
69	- Totals: item count, subtotal, shipping cost (default $0), tax line items (per locale), grand total, duties/taxes disclaimer (CFD-016)
70	- Promo code field with success and error states (CFD-017)
71	- Edit items from summary → returns customer to cart; checkout re-enters at delivery step regardless of prior progress. Re-starting checkout on basket update is a platform constraint and cannot be customised (CFD-018)
72	- If an item goes OOS during checkout: checkout button disabled; warning displayed in close proximity to the unavailable item; customer must remove manually — no auto-removal (CFD-019)
73	- No product recommendations in checkout or order summary — only in mini-cart and cart (CFD-021)
74	- International orders (non-AU storefront): Global-e owns and displays all order totals. AU storefront is the exception — all AU orders (including Oceania international: NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) are processed within SFCC and do not hand off to Global-e (CFD-020)
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 6. Delivery Address (CFD-023 – CFD-033)
79	
80	- **Address autocomplete: Google Maps API** (replaces PCA Predict/Loqate) — CFD-023, CFD-030
81	- Single Google API contract, configured per storefront, returning country-appropriate results (CFD-030)
82	- Graceful degradation to manual entry if Google API unavailable, with country and state-level validation to prevent orders from unsupported markets — never hard-block checkout (CFD-031)
83	- PO Box and Parcel Locker addresses blocked at entry and at submission (CFD-024)
84	- Locale-specific address formats: AU, US, UK, EU domestic (CFD-025)
85	- Guest users: country and mobile prefix pre-populated per storefront (both editable); all other fields blank (CFD-027)
86	- Registered customers: select from saved addresses, edit, or add new (CFD-028)
87	- New address saved to account on order completion, synced to Omneo via bidirectional MuleSoft webhook. New address does **not** replace the existing default — customer can opt to make it default (CFD-029)
88	- Carrier label automation (Shippit, Ordoro) is OMS-level and not invoked from SFCC at checkout; delivery address is passed to MuleSoft at order creation for downstream fulfilment routing (CFD-032)
89	- No order splitting — all items delivered to same address (CFD-033)
90	- Global-e owns delivery address capture and validation for international storefronts (US international, ME, EU international, HK) (CFD-026)
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 7. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CFD-034 – CFD-048, OM-012 – OM-016)
95	
96	- Boutique list + Google Maps interactive map at delivery step; no boutique selected by default (CFD-034)
97	- Boutique details: name, address, availability (Available/Unavailable per item + selected size), opening hours (CFD-035)
98	- Only show boutiques within the customer's storefront region; alphabetical; outlets at bottom; default selection per region (CFD-036)
99	- Order summary updates to show Collect in Boutique with boutique name, per-item availability, $0 shipping (CFD-037)
100	- Items unavailable at selected boutique: prompt to move to wishlist, remove from cart, or select different delivery. **All items must be available at the boutique to proceed** (CFD-038)
101	- Guest attempting wishlist from BOPIS prompted to sign in (CFD-039). Guest wishlist without login is out of scope (enhancement).
102	- Collection name (first/last) required; must match ID; not pre-populated at launch; not saved to account (CFD-040, CFD-047)
103	- Informational/disclaimer text including processing times and contact email (CFD-041)
104	- If customer switches back to home delivery, previously entered home delivery address is preserved (CFD-042)
105	- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft only when BOPIS screen or Find in Boutique drawer is opened — not on general browsing (CFD-043). No buffer stock applied to boutique inventory (OM-032)
106	- Store hours from Google Business via stored Google Place ID, with manual override in SFCC (CFD-044)
107	- BOPIS eligibility controlled by a store attribute in SFCC, set per boutique and revisable seasonally (CFD-045 — Confirmed; seeding mechanism still open, see Open Items)
108	- States, regions, or countries with all stores BOPIS-disabled are hidden from the boutique selector (CFD-046)
109	- Collect in Boutique is **not displayed** as a delivery option when the cart contains a digital gift card (CFD-048, updated wording)
110	- Gift card products excluded from BOPIS (OM-014, OM-016)
111	- Full payment at placement for BOPIS orders (OM-012)
112	- Selected boutique ID + 'collect from boutique' flag passed to NewStore via MuleSoft; NewStore owns BOPIS fulfilment from that point (OM-013)
113	- BOPIS order statuses in My Account: Processing → Ready to Collect → Collected / Cancelled (OM-015)
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 8. Delivery Methods (CFD-049 – CFD-057, OM-008 – OM-011)
118	
119	- Delivery methods configured per storefront in SFCC Business Manager (CFD-049, OM-008)
120	- Each method shows: name, EDD timeframe (Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) widget for domestic; Global-e for international), cost (CFD-050, OM-009)
121	- Free shipping thresholds configurable in Business Manager **independently per delivery method and per storefront** (e.g. Ground free above $1000, Express free above $2000) (OM-010). Eligible VIC groups get free shipping regardless of order value (CFD-051)
122	- Selected delivery method passed to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft; NewStore owns all downstream carrier selection, dispatch, and label generation (CFD-052, OM-007, OM-011)
123	- Delivery method disclaimer text with direct outbound email link for assistance (CFD-053)
124	- Uber same-day delivery on AU only at launch, restricted to specific eligible zones within Australia (CFD-056); expansion to other regions pending NewStore capability
125	- Global-e owns delivery method selection for international orders outside Oceania (CFD-055)
126	- International order data flow: Global-e → SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore OMS (CFD-057)
127	
128	---
129	
130	## 9. Billing Address (CFD-058 – CFD-066)
131	
132	- Billing address section presented within checkout (CFD-058)
133	- Google Maps API autocomplete (same as delivery; replaces Loqate) with manual fallback (CFD-059)
134	- Single Google API contract per storefront; graceful degradation to manual entry if API unavailable; no hard block (CFD-065)
135	- Pre-filled from delivery address by default; same-as-shipping checkbox pre-selected for both guest and registered (CFD-061)
136	- Supports billing address in a different country to delivery address on domestic storefronts (CFD-062)
137	- Locale-specific formats for AU, US, UK, EU domestic (CFD-060)
138	- Save billing address option pre-selected for logged-in customers (CFD-063); saved to SFCC and synced bidirectionally to Omneo (Omneo is master) via MuleSoft webhook (CFD-064)
139	- Global-e owns billing address capture and validation for international storefronts outside Oceania (CFD-066)
140	- **Company Name and VAT/Tax ID fields at billing (CFD-067 — Confirmed 2026-06-24):** Phase 1 presents two optional fields — Company Name and VAT/Tax ID — at the billing step for EU Domestic, EU International, and UK storefronts. Both fields are optional with no validation at launch. Signed off by Rebecca (2026-06-24), aligned with Finance. Future release (out of Phase 1 scope): fields become mandatory for company purchases; Avalara VAT ID validation will be introduced at that point, with the system reverting the order to a personal purchase if a valid VAT ID is not provided.
141	
142	---
143	
144	## 10. Payments (PAY-001 – PAY-067)
145	
146	### Launch payment methods (all domestic storefronts via Adyen)
147	- Credit/debit card — Visa, Mastercard, Amex (PAY-002)
148	- PayPal via Adyen with redirect and return; billing address pre-populated from PayPal callback (PAY-003, PAY-023)
149	- Gift cards (GiveX) — balance check flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool); redemption flows via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft (GC-039). See [giftcards.md §11](./giftcards.md) for the full architecture note.
150	- Retail Rewards (AP21 VIP balance) — see section 12
151	
152	### Targeting August 2026 (confirmed in scope, not launch)
153	- Apple Pay Express (mini bag) (PAY-004) and Apple Pay at checkout (PAY-005) — all domestic storefronts
154	- Google Pay and Google Pay Express (PAY-006) — all domestic storefronts
155	- Klarna BNPL (PAY-007) — AU and US only
156	
157	### Payment rules
158	- Available methods presented at the payment step, configured per storefront in Business Manager (PAY-001)
159	- Global-e owns all payment for international orders — Adyen/PayPal are NOT invoked for Global-e orders (PAY-009)
160	- Full payment options: card, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, gift card (digital or physical), credit note, Retail Rewards full balance (PAY-010)
161	- Split payment: gift card, credit note, or Retail Rewards combined with any external payment method (PAY-011)
162	- Gift card cannot be purchased using a gift card as payment; gift card payment option removed at checkout when a gift card is in cart (PAY-011a, PAY-011b)
163	- Saved payment methods displayed at checkout for returning customers (PAY-017); opt-in to save ("Save this card to your account for faster checkout", unchecked by default) (PAY-018); manageable from My Account showing card type, last four digits, expiry sourced from Adyen via token reference (PAY-019); removal in My Account deletes the corresponding token in Adyen (PAY-020); raw card data never stored in SFCC — tokens in Adyen only (PAY-021)
164	- **Saved-card CVV re-entry (PAY-022, Confirmed):** the PWA requires the customer to re-enter the CVV/CVC for any previously saved card at the point of payment. The 3DS re-challenge decision is owned by Adyen (out of PWA boundary) — the PWA does not control whether 3DS re-prompts. **Security handling:** the CVV is never logged (no `console.*`, Sentry, GTM/dataLayer, or MRT access log) and never persisted client-side (no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB/cookies) — it lives in React state only, is cleared on submit/unmount, and is sent only in the POST body. (MFA on account login was noted as a complementary control but is not part of this requirement.) The CVV-on-saved-cards enhancement (ENH-019) is now Cancelled — the capability is not lost, it has been folded into this confirmed requirement; only the Adyen-side CVC configuration remains open (see Open Items).
165	  - *Additional scenario (Adyen-confirmed 2026-06-25):* when a returning customer with a saved card enters a **new/unsaved shipping address**, the checkout must also prompt for CVC re-entry at the address step before the customer can proceed. Triggered by address change, distinct from the payment-step re-entry above. Implementation detail and the paired Adyen Custom Risk Rule are in the Adyen integration doc §10.
166	- 3DS authentication inline via Adyen Drop-In — no redirect away from checkout (PAY-045)
167	- Adyen RevenueProtect fraud screening on every domestic order — all fraud rule management in Adyen; SFCC passes data and responds to outcome only (PAY-013, PAY-041)
168	- Customer group attribute passed to Adyen for group-specific fraud risk scoring; custom fraud rules implemented as shared rules targeted by country/market (PAY-042)
169	- Shopper/order data passed to Adyen: name, email, phone, billing address, delivery address, registered country (PAY-042a). isGiftCard=TRUE flag when gift card payment included (PAY-043)
170	- Orders containing a gift card purchase (physical or digital) placed into fraud review by Adyen — fulfilment and gift card code delivery withheld until review resolved (PAY-044)
171	- Fraud webhook notifications routed via MuleSoft; SFCC has no role in fraud hold monitoring or timing (PAY-046)
172	- On Ops approval in Adyen, release routed via MuleSoft to NewStore; SFCC reflects updated NewStore order status (PAY-050)
173	- On Ops rejection in Adyen, NewStore cancels via MuleSoft and refund initiated via Adyen to original payment method; SFCC reflects cancelled status (PAY-051)
174	- Address mismatch: error/warning before order completion. Express payment methods (Apple Pay Express, Google Pay Express) are rejected at Adyen level if the address doesn't match the storefront region. The system will not offer ship-to countries outside the storefront region (PAY-015)
175	- No retry limit — Adyen Drop-In manages (PAY-014)
176	- Payment failure: clear error messaging; allow retry or alternative method without losing order data (PAY-008)
177	- Pay by Link via Adyen for manual/CS orders (PAY-016)
178	- Level 2/3 payment data passed to Adyen for interchange fee optimisation (PAY-012)
179	- Packaging defaults and available options per payment method are configurable per storefront in Business Manager; option labels/descriptions editable per storefront (PAY-024, PAY-025, PAY-026)
180	
181	### Tax and duty display (PAY-053, PAY-055 – PAY-067)
182	- Mini-cart: subtotal with incl/excl tax label per storefront (PAY-055)
183	- Cart and checkout: itemised tax line items, subtotal (incl/excl tax) and tax amount — labels per storefront (PAY-056, PAY-057)
184	- Tax and duties shown as separate line items, never combined (PAY-058)
185	- DDP/DDU messaging on PDP, mini-cart, and cart per applicable countries (PAY-059, PAY-060, PAY-061)
186	- Duties and Taxes hyperlink within the checkout disclaimer for applicable countries (PAY-062)
187	- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US and HK); label passed to Narvar for returns/tracking (PAY-063)
188	- Domestic vs. international determined by customer's selected shipping country, not IP (PAY-053)
189	- **Narvar payload:** for multi-quantity line items, pass unit tax value divided by quantity — not the total line tax (PAY-064)
190	- **HS codes:** received from AP21 (generated by Avalara, stored in AP21 custom fields per country). For international orders via Global-e, SFCC passes HS codes to Global-e. For cross-border orders on domestic storefronts (e.g. NZ on AU), SFCC stores and passes HS codes to Avalara (PAY-066; transition to Global-e for Oceania not yet confirmed)
191	- **Tax engines:** Avalara for US domestic (variable state tax), New Zealand (GST/VAT + duties), New Caledonia (GST/VAT + duties). All other domestic storefronts use SFCC native tax tables (PAY-067; transition to Global-e for Oceania not yet confirmed)
192	
193	---
194	
195	## 11. Cross-Border / International Checkout (PAY-053, PAY-054, CFD-020)
196	
197	*For which storefronts are domestic vs. Global-e, AU Oceania scope, and URL prefixes, see AGENTS.md "Multi-site & Routing".*
198	
199	Frontend-specific checkout responsibilities:
200	- International customers are routed to a Zimmermann checkout page that **embeds the Global-e hosted checkout in an iframe** from both mini-bag and cart (PAY-054). The shopper remains on `www.zimmermann.com` — this is an iframe embed, not a full-page redirect.
201	- Domestic vs. international determined by the customer's **selected shipping country**, not IP (PAY-053)
202	- Do not attempt to replicate Global-e UI; do not render a partial/hybrid checkout state
203	- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (confirmed — REG-041, 2026-05-05):** SFCC holds all price books, including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. Mechanism confirmed (PRC-34 to PRC-43, REG-041 confirmed 2026-05-05; REG-040 retired 2026-05-05).
204	
205	---
206	
207	## 12. Retail Rewards (PAY-027 – PAY-040)
208	
209	- Available for Gold VIP and Platinum VIP customers on domestic storefronts only
210	- Automatically applied at payment step (full balance); customer can remove. Partial redemption applies only where balance exceeds cart value. Can be combined with credit cards, gift cards, credit notes, and promo codes (PAY-027)
211	- Displayed as a separate named line item in the order summary (e.g. "DISCOUNT | GOLD VIP - 10% OFF"), showing the amount deducted from subtotal (PAY-028)
212	- Additional payment required if balance does not cover full order — credit card, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, gift card, or credit note (in-store or online) (PAY-029)
213	- No additional payment required where Retail Rewards balance covers the full order total (PAY-030)
214	- Real-time AP21 validation at point of automatic application, to prevent applying the same balance across concurrent orders (PAY-031)
215	- Retail Rewards are a *voucher payment method*, not a discount. US: applied before tax (Avalara handles variable state tax). All other domestic storefronts: applied post-tax (PAY-032)
216	- AP21 unavailability: inform customer, allow alternative payment method without losing the order (PAY-033)
217	- My Account dashboard displays the customer's Loyalty Status tier name with a brief tier benefits description (PAY-034) and total available Retail Rewards balance, sum of unredeemed vouchers, updated on every login (PAY-035)
218	- Refunds returned via the original payment method; redeemed Retail Rewards balance returned to the customer's Retail Rewards account for the same value used (PAY-036)
219	- My Orders shows Retail Rewards balance and transaction history for eligible Gold/Platinum VIPs (PAY-037)
220	- My Account shows a breakdown table of individual vouchers — Description, Amount Issued, Amount Used, Amount Remaining, Expiry Date — ordered by soonest expiry (PAY-038)
221	- HK, ME, EU International: Retail Rewards **cannot** be redeemed online. My Account shows a message directing VIP clients to Client Services (PAY-039)
222	- Retail Rewards is a separate payment mechanism from GiveX gift cards — a single checkout may invoke both a GiveX call and an AP21 Retail Rewards call independently (PAY-040)
223	
224	---
225	
226	## 13. Order Confirmation Page (CFD-068 – CFD-072)
227	
228	- Confirmation page displays: order number, items, delivery address, delivery method, order total, EDD via Narvar (CFD-068).
229	- Guest customers offered account creation on the confirmation page (CFD-070, pending guest journey sign-off).
230	- Domestic order confirmation email triggered via Narvar (includes EDD). Shipping confirmation emails also managed by Narvar — not triggered from SFCC (CFD-069).
231	- International order confirmation page: SFCC owns the page display but populates it with Global-e order data (CFD-071); international confirmation email sent by Global-e directly.
232	- Order and customer data passed to OMS (AP21 / NewStore) via MuleSoft and to Omneo at order placement (CFD-072).
233	
234	OMS export mechanics (OM-001..007, OM-036), order tracking surface in My Account (OM-015, OM-017..020, OM-035), and inventory / buffer-stock display (OM-021..034) all live in [orderManagement.md](./orderManagement.md).
235	
236	---
237	
238	## 14. Order on Behalf Of / OOBO (RRC-019 – RRC-029)
239	
240	CS agents can access the storefront as a specific customer from Business Manager, with the ability to:
241	- Browse catalogue, add to cart, apply/remove coupons
242	- Select delivery addresses and shipping method
243	- Pay via stored Adyen token or Pay-by-Link (PAY-016)
244	
245	OOBO orders are attributed to the customer record and pass through the standard SFCC pipeline. An agent identifier is attached for reporting. All standard checkout rules apply (tax, inventory, shipping). Full OOBO requirements set is still TBC.
246	
247	---
248	
249	## 15. Error States
250	
251	- Form validation errors must be inline and blocking
252	- Payment failures must return users to the review/payment step without losing order state (PAY-008)
253	- No silent retries; no auto-submission
254	- OOS at checkout: blocked with inline warning near unavailable item; customer must remove manually (CFD-019)
255	
256	---
257	
258	## 16. Open Items
259	
260	- **Omneo profile match at guest checkout (CFD-008):** Originally strikethrough/replaced. Latest wording: if an Omneo-only profile is found (no SFCC password), prompt to create a password to activate the account; if SFCC account exists, prompt to log in or reset; customer may dismiss and continue as guest. Pending Customer Workshop sign-off.
261	- **Social login (CFD-011 strikethrough; new requirement):** Apple/Google confirmed in scope for launch per Enhancement Log ("Go-Live" tag); implementation details still Open.
262	- **Guest account-creation on confirmation page (CFD-070):** Dependent on the guest checkout decision; not existing functionality. Awaiting sign-off.
263	- **BOPIS eligibility seeding (CFD-045):** SFCC store attribute confirmed as mechanism; pending sign-off on whether values are seeded pre-build or maintained by merchandising. Sign-off date not yet recorded.
264	- **General address-validation review (CFD-024, review request):** CFD-024's PO Box / Parcel Locker block remains Confirmed (documented in §6). A separate VR/RT comment raises an enhancement question — *"Current magento behaviour lets a user checkout with a very random address with no error messaging. Can this be reviewed?"* — i.e. broader address-validity checking beyond PO Box / Parcel Locker. Not yet scoped; pending review.
265	- **CVC-on-saved-card Adyen configuration (ENH-019, 9th-June note):** PAY-022 CVV re-entry is confirmed PWA behaviour, but the CVC-on-saved-card configuration must be confirmed with Adyen. Pending Adyen confirmation.
266	- **Adyen dynamic checkout / payment-method display (ENH-020):** dynamically adjust payment method display and design per user profile/behaviour, including Adyen A/B testing of payment-method presentation. In scope for go-live pending confirmation from Tim; hard dependency on Adyen delivering the capability; still to be sized.
267	- **Fraud hold scope (PAY-047, PAY-048, PAY-049):** SFCC scope clarified — order created and passed to MuleSoft on payment authorisation; NewStore holds inventory; fraud hold duration and customer-facing messaging suppression sit outside SFCC. Sign-off pending.
268	- **HS codes and tax engine for Oceania (PAY-066, PAY-067):** Correct for Oceania today; transition to Global-e not yet confirmed.
269	- **Order Management open items** (OM-002 export gating, OM-017/018 NewStore status taxonomy, OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO logic) live in [orderManagement.md §6](./orderManagement.md).
270	- **OOBO full requirement set:** Not yet finalised — Pay by Link recommended to stay in Adyen (PAY-016 sign-off pending the wider OOBO scope).
271	- **BOPIS billing-address step:** Whether billing address is a required step in the BOPIS flow not explicitly stated in requirements. Clarify before implementing.
272	
273	---
274	
275	## 17. Explicit Non-Goals (at launch)
276	
277	- Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna (August 2026)
278	- Social login implementation (confirmed in scope, but implementation Open)
279	- Checkout A/B testing logic

281	- Guest wishlist from BOPIS (post-launch enhancement)
282	- Order Management non-goals (shipment-level tracking display, BM-side buffer-stock authoring UI, loyalty-tier prioritisation in back-in-stock queue) — see [orderManagement.md §7](./orderManagement.md).
